title: Title Writing Guidelines
content: Titles should be concise, factual, and descriptive. A good title includes: product name, key differentiating feature, and an important specification where relevant. Titles must not be keyword-stuffed, written in ALL CAPS, or contain more than 200 characters. Do not include price, promotional phrases, or unverifiable claims in the title.

title: Description Formatting Standards
content: Descriptions should be structured clearly. Use short paragraphs or bullet points for features. Begin with a brief overview of the product or service, followed by key features or specifications. Avoid excessive repetition. The description must add value beyond the title — do not simply restate the title. Minimum useful description length is 50 characters.

title: Approved Brand Language
content: Use clear, simple, buyer-focused language. Write as if explaining the product to a knowledgeable buyer, not a general audience. Avoid jargon unless the product is technical and the category warrants it. Positive, benefit-oriented language is encouraged. Avoid hype words: amazing, incredible, unbelievable, revolutionary, game-changer.

title: Prohibited Hype and Exaggerated Language
content: The following categories of language are prohibited: urgency-inducing language without a genuine limited offer (e.g. 'act now', 'limited time only'), superlatives without evidence (e.g. 'the most advanced ever made'), exaggerated adjectives (e.g. 'mind-blowing', 'revolutionary'), and emotional manipulation tactics.

title: Attribute and Specification Standards
content: Product attributes should use standard units and naming conventions. Numeric values must include units (e.g. '500g', '15.6 inches', '10,000 mAh'). Boolean features should be stated clearly (e.g. 'Water resistant: Yes'). Attribute keys should be consistent with category norms. Avoid vague attributes like 'Quality: High' without supporting evidence.
